scenes.voice: Hey kids! Today we're building a place value chart the Indian way. It helps us read and write really big numbers, all the way up to crores. Ready to explore?
Every number starts with ones, tens, and hundreds. In the number 4 5 6, the 6 is in the ones place, the 5 is in the tens place, and the 4 is in the hundreds place. Each spot has its own value!
After hundreds comes thousands, then ten-thousands. In the Indian system we group numbers in pairs after the first three digits. So 12,345 is read as 12 thousand, 3 hundred and 45.
Next come lakhs! One lakh is 1 followed by 5 zeros, written as 1,00,000. Ten lakhs is 10,00,000. We write a comma after every two digits once we pass the thousands place.

One crore is 1 followed by 7 zeros, written as 1,00,00,000. In the international system, the same number is called 10 million. Lakhs and crores are the Indian names, while thousands and millions are used internationally — same numbers, different names!
How many zeros are there in one lakh — 1,00,000?

Amazing work! You now know the Indian place value chart from ones all the way to crores, and how it compares to thousands and millions. Keep practicing reading big numbers — you're becoming a place value expert!
